text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The United Nations Development Programme has agreed to back a womens' rights project with $1.5 million.

-- Vietnam and China are to open another passenger train link through the border check-point in Lao Cai province, about 300 km (188 miles) northwest of Hanoi. An inaugural date has yet to be set by the two countries' governments.

-- Iraq will buy rice and tea from Vietnam over the next four years, visiting Iraqi Minister for Trade Mohammed Mehdi Saleh told Vietnam's Minister for Agriculture and Rural Development, Nguyen Cong Tan.
-- The Market Management Board of Ho Chi Minh City has warned that a large volume of canned food which has passed its sell-by date is appearing on the market.

-- Exe Design Co Ltd of Japan will transfer all its 70 percent stake in a $58.5 million hotel project in Hanoi to the Sakura Ha Noi Plaza Investment Co Ltd of Hong Kong, the Ministry of Planning and Investment said.
-- Do Muoi, Secretary General of the Communist Party, has called on the Nhan dan daily to be a political and ideological flag of the party and be useful and more interesting.
-- The Southern Steel Company expects its output of sheet steel in 1996 to be 280,000 tonnes, a five-fold increase from 1991.
-- State budget revenue had reached 83 percent of a target set for the whole year by the end of November.
-- Dong Xuan market, the biggest market in Hanoi, is scheduled to be reopen on December 19 after being razed by a huge fire in 1994.
-- A total of 3,250 HIV carriers have been reported in Ho Chi Minh city, 80 percent of whom are drug addicts.
